principle_violations.reason: The Order class is responsible for managing order details as well as having methods related to changing its status, which is a separate concern.
principle_violations.suggestion: Consider refactoring the status management out of Order into a separate class, like OrderStatus, that manages order states.

original_code: public void setStatus(String status) { this.status = status; }
suggestion_code: public class OrderStatus { private String status; public OrderStatus() { this.status = 'open'; } public void setStatus(String status) { this.status = status; } public String getStatus() { return status; } }

principle_violations.reason: If a new type of item or payment method needs to be added, the Order and PaymentProcessor classes would need to be modified, violating the open/closed principle.
principle_violations.suggestion: Create interfaces for item management and payment processing, allowing new implementations to be added without modifying existing code.

original_code: public void addItem(String name, int quantity, double price) { this.items.add(name); this.quantities.add(quantity); this.prices.add(price); }
public void pay(Order order, String securityCode) { System.out.println('Processing payment'); System.out.println('Verifying security code: ' + securityCode); order.setStatus('paid'); }
suggestion_code: public interface ItemManagement { void addItem(String name, int quantity, double price); } public interface PaymentMethod { void pay(Order order, String securityCode); }
